The category whose objects are triples $(A,I,\gamma)$ consisting of a commutative ring $A$, ideal $I$, and divided power structure $\gamma$ on $I$, with morphisms preserving these structures has all limits and they agree with
limits in the category of rings.
conclusions:

limits in the category of rings.
semantic_review_note: The category of divided-power rings (A,I,γ) with PD-preserving homomorphisms has all limits, and their underlying rings are the corresponding ring-theoretic limits. The reconstruction states the full object/morphism convention, not merely existence of products.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-a-version-of-brown}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the category of divided power rings. Let
$F : \mathcal{C} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists a cardinal $\kappa$ such that for every
$f \in F(A, I, \gamma)$ there exists a morphism
$(A', I', \gamma') \to (A, I, \gamma)$ of $\mathcal{C}$ such that $f$
is the image of $f' \in F(A', I', \gamma')$ and $|A'| \leq \kappa$, and
\item $F$ commutes with limits.
\end{enumerate}
Then $F$ is representable, i.e., there exists an object $(B, J, \delta)$
of $\mathcal{C}$ such that
$$
F(A, I, \gamma) = \Hom_\mathcal{C}((B, J, \delta), (A, I, \gamma))
$$
functorially in $(A, I, \gamma)$.

semantic_review_note: A set-valued covariant functor on PD rings is representable if it commutes with limits and has a cardinal bound κ allowing every element to be pulled back from a PD ring A' of size ≤κ. original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-colimits}
The category of divided power rings has all colimits.
statement: The category whose objects are triples $(A,I,\gamma)$ consisting of a commutative ring $A$, ideal $I$, and divided power structure $\gamma$ on $I$, with morphisms preserving these structures has all colimits.
conclusions: The category whose objects are triples $(A,I,\gamma)$ consisting of a commutative ring $A$, ideal $I$, and divided power structure $\gamma$ on $I$, with morphisms preserving these structures has all colimits.
semantic_review_note: The category of PD rings, whose morphisms preserve ideals and divided powers, possesses all colimits. The final restates the category and the existence conclusion, without asserting they agree with ring colimits (only limits have that extra clause).
